column1: # One case per line: a format, a TAB, an argument kind, a TAB, the
# argument. Kinds: d signed, u unsigned, f floating, s string, c one
# character, n no argument, w "width:number" for %*d. Nothing here says
# what the right answer is - the host's own snprintf decides, and this
# project's has to agree with it byte for byte. See tools/printf-test.sh.
# One conversion per case, because the argument's C type comes from the
# format and the driver types exactly one.
# ---- the h and hh rows, which are why this file exists (M98: %hx of a
# ---- negative short printed the whole promotion) ----
# ---- the l and ll and z rows ----
# ---- M98: the # flag, which was missing entirely ----
# GCC's dwarf2out emits `.cfi_personality %#x,` - a formatter that did
# not know `#` wrote the three characters %#x into the assembly file and
# the machine's own `as` refused what it produced. Nothing in this file
# had a `#` in it before these lines, which is the case list's own
# lesson: a differential test is only as good as the cases somebody
